name: T-80BVM

image.license: See Commons file page for license

cost.display: No clean public unit price; produced via modernization of Soviet-era T-80 hulls

characteristics: Strength: Best cold-weather/high-altitude performance among Russian MBTs due to turbine engine; heavily upgraded over base T-80
Limitation: Turbine engine has poor fuel economy and higher maintenance burden than diesel T-72/T-90 family; Russia lost effectively its entire pre-war T-80 fleet (~1,200) over the course of the war
Estimated quantity available: Grew from ~100 to ~280 in fielded units by late 2025 (Janes), rebuilt from deep storage stock rather than new production
employment_notes: Entire pre-war T-80 inventory (~1,200) has been expended and replaced by continued modernization of stored hulls — the clearest single data point for how thoroughly Soviet-era stockpiles are being consumed
contrast_vs_traditional: Like the Abrams, the T-80BVM's gas-turbine engine trades fuel economy for speed and cold-weather reliability — a Cold War tradeoff made for a rapid maneuver war across open terrain. Reactivated from strategic reserve rather than built new, it now fights under the same constraint as every other armored asset here: whichever side controls the lower sky over the sector sets how close it can be positioned, not the tank's own speed or protection.
